claims.text: Pulumi programs can reference existing Terraform state files (Terraform remote state) to read their outputs.
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs.
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly from Pulumi.
Terraform HCL code can be converted to Pulumi code.
Terraform and Pulumi deployments can be orchestrated together.

In the multi-stack example, a core infrastructure stack that 'could be Terraform' is consumed from a Pulumi application stack via `pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` and `getOutput("vpcId")` (a StackReference reads outputs of a Pulumi stack; the core stack exports `vpc`, not `vpcId`).
`new pulumi.StackReference(name)` has a `getOutput(name)` method that returns a stack output.

The `@pulumi/terraform` package exposes `terraform.state.S3Reference` (a class constructed with `bucket` and `key` arguments and offering `getOutput(name)`) for referencing Terraform state stored in S3.
`pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference` is accessible from the `pulumi` namespace imported via `import * as pulumi from "@pulumi/pulumi/automation"`.
The `aws.ecs.Cluster` resource accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` (value `"DEFAULT"`) properties.
`pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
State ownership can be transferred from Terraform to Pulumi gradually, resource-by-resource.

The `pulumi import` CLI takes the form `pulumi import <type-token> <name> <id>`, e.g. `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`, `aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet`, and `aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster` are valid resource type tokens.
Pulumi provides an import API that can be used programmatically within a Pulumi program to import resources.
Pulumi policies can enforce infrastructure policies across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.

The `@pulumi/policy` package exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`, and policies use `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"` and a `validateResource` callback with signature `(resource, args, reportViolation)`.
`aws.s3.Bucket` has an `acl` property that can be set to `public-read` or `public-read-write`.
The Pulumi Automation API allows embedding Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.

The Pulumi Automation API is imported from `@pulumi/pulumi/automation` and provides `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack({stackName, projectName, program})`, `stack.setConfig(key, {value})`, `stack.up({onOutput})`, and an `outputs` property on the up result.
Component resources can wrap Terraform-managed infrastructure behind the scenes, leaving the complexity of multi-tool management to the platform team rather than development teams.
`pulumi.ComponentResource` subclasses call `super(type, name, {}, opts)` with `pulumi.ComponentResourceOptions`, and use `registerOutputs` to register outputs.
Developers can create WebApplication component resources in Pulumi without knowing they depend on Terraform-managed resources.
